name: Gibbs’s statistical ensemble framework
description: Gibbs systematized statistical mechanics using distributions over hypothetical systems.

impact.note: A systematic recasting of statistical mechanics that physicists already practised; modern classical and quantum statistical mechanics use its framework.

date.basis: Year of the dated publication, or a broad historian-estimated composition interval; no first discovery claimed.

events.statement: Gibbs published Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics in 1902.

evidence.supports: The 1902 preface describes collections of systems and names Boltzmann among the founders.
The history discusses Gibbs’s canonical and microcanonical ensembles and their antecedents.
The 1902 preface describes collections of systems and names Boltzmann among the founders.

earliest_record.rationale: Dated witness within the inspected evidence; not a global-priority claim.

caveats: Gibbs credited Maxwell, Clausius and Boltzmann; the ensemble framework was not created from nothing in 1902. This is a classical treatment, not modern quantum statistical mechanics. His preface credits Boltzmann generally and identifies an 1871 paper; it does not by itself establish a direct dependency on the separate 1877 result.
